title: Put a tall box away in a cupboard it only fits into lying down
instruction: Put the cereal box away in the low cupboard.
context: Stocking low shelves and packing often means laying a tall package on its side. A top-down gripper that only turns about the vertical cannot do that by grasping; it has to tip the box over with a push and then slide it in.
setup: A light grey countertop (90 x 100 cm) covers the table. A wooden low cupboard with an open front stands 14 cm right of the arm bases' midline: inside it is 20.8 cm deep, 23.6 cm wide and 9.4 cm high, with its open front 45.5 cm in front of the bases; its top is set back 3 cm from the front of the side walls. A cereal box (cardboard, 18 cm tall, 8 cm wide, 5 cm deep, 350 g) stands upright 26 cm in front of the bases, 14 cm right of the midline, its wide faces toward the robot and the cupboard. A wooden fruit bowl, a jar and a red tea towel lie on the left of the counter.
scoring: 1.0 with the box lying on its side (tilted 60 degrees or more from upright) and wholly inside the cupboard (between the side walls, behind the front of the walls, 1 cm tolerance). 0.5 if it lies on its side with at least half its length inside the cupboard. 0 otherwise, including standing upright, off the counter or outside the cupboard's width.
reset_notes: Stand the box back upright on its mark.
fidelity: Rigid bodies only; the cereal box is a solid block and the cupboard is fixed. Every surface has the same rubber-like friction (1.2).
